name: Gas turbine generator
summary: A combustion gas turbine coupled to a synchronous generator, often through a gearbox, shown as a generating unit.
description: A gas turbine generator uses a continuous-combustion turbine to drive a synchronous generator, often through a reduction gearbox for smaller industrial machines. Units range from microturbines of tens of kilowatts with high-speed alternators and inverters, up to large industrial turbines feeding a medium-voltage bus.

The drawing usually shows a turbine glyph, a trapezoid widening in the direction of flow, joined by a shaft line to the generator circle. A generator step-up transformer, generator breaker and neutral earthing equipment follow on the single-line diagram.

Microturbines with high-speed alternators produce high-frequency output that must pass through a rectifier and inverter, so check whether a converter sits between the machine and the bus. The symbol does not state fuel, start method or ambient derating.
readingNotes: A trapezoid on the shaft line indicates the turbine; a gearbox may be drawn as a small box between turbine and generator.
Look for a converter stage on microturbine packages.
drawingChecklist: State ISO rating and site derating.
Show gearbox, generator breaker and earthing.
Reference start system and black-start capability.
distinction: A gas turbine is a continuous-combustion rotating prime mover; a gas engine is reciprocating.
